New FCC Rules May Prevent Installing OpenWRT on WiFi Routers

I use ddwrt and I love it. It pisses me off that original firmware included with these routers are crap and now we may lose the ability to upload whatever firmware we want. Hell I just did it to my father in law's router because he needed to use a VPN and the original firmware did not have that capability.
How do I do this myself before it's too late?

DD-WRT has a ton of walkthroughs and is stupid simple to instal and use. OpenWRT is a little more complex (but more customizable), and there are a half dozen other alternatives out there that are off-shoots (Tomato comes to mind, I know there are others). Simply start here with DD-WRT:

http://www.dd-wrt.com/site/support/faq

Get the router model that you have and go to the ddwrt website. They will have a list of routers that are compatible. Download the recommended version of the ddwrt firmware. I download it to my desktop. Then go to your routers administrator page and click on firmware update. Point to the location the you saved the file to and that's pretty much it. When your router boots back up it will be a brand new and more powerful interface. I'm thinking about downloading as many firmware versions as I can right now. Let me know if need more help. You should know that the process is not fool proof and you could ultimately brick your router. I've been using ddwrt for many years and have "upgraded" many routers. I've never bricked one.
I'm really interested in the prospect of this. In what sense does it upgrade your router? I'm willing to risk mine.

It gives you more functionality and allows you to adjust settings that you wouldn't normally be able to with stock firmware. Like the article said, you could increase the power of your router's wireless signal, create a wired bridge, change to channels that wouldn't be available to you. Certain versions of ddwrt will have VPN servers built in. You can create hot spots although I'm not sure how that feature is useful. I use mine mainly for the VPN capabilities. It's either upload ddwrt to a cheap router and make it perform like a 200 dollar router or by the 200 dollar router.

I don't know too much about all the features of ddwrt you should definitely check out the ddwrt wiki. Give me a second and I'll edit this comment with a link.

Edit: here it is. http://www.dd-wrt.com/wiki/index.php/Main_Page

Don't use DD-WRT if you can. It's really a bunch of unstable hacks based on binary blobs. OpenWRT is in a different class compared to it. DD-WRT has more device support, but that's because they're willing to cut corners (using closed source drivers and components)
